validated_results.title: The risk factors of prostate cancer: a multicentric case-control study in Iran.
validated_results.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
validated_results.reason: Original multicentric case-control study reporting an odds ratio for dietary lycopene consumption and incident clinicopathologically confirmed prostate cancer.

extraction.population: Men with incident, clinicopathologically confirmed prostate cancer and hospital controls without malignant disease

sample_size.excerpt: Prostate cancer (PC), in Iran, is the third most frequently diagnosed visceral cancer among men and the seventh most common underlying cause of cancer mortality. We evaluated the relation between speculated factors and PC risk using data from a multicentric case-control study conducted in Iran from 2005 to 2007 on 130 cases of incident, clinicopathologically confirmed PC, and 75 controls admitted to the same network of hospitals without any malignant disease.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 130 + 75 = 205

cases.excerpt: We evaluated the relation between speculated factors and PC risk using data from a multicentric case-control study conducted in Iran from 2005 to 2007 on 130 cases of incident, clinicopathologically confirmed PC, and 75 controls admitted to the same network of hospitals without any malignant disease.

effect_size.excerpt: Increasing in dietary consumption of lycopene and fat was associated with declined (OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.09-2.12) and increased (OR: 2.38, 95% CI: 0.29-19.4) PC development, respectively. Other factors including educational level, marriage status, dietary meat consumption, vasectomy and smoking have not been shown to affect PC risk in the Iranian population.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Increasing in dietary consumption of lycopene and fat was associated with declined (OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.09-2.12) and increased (OR: 2.38, 95% CI: 0.29-19.4) PC development, respectively.
